binding_resource_stop_rule: Binding resource stop rule: Binding construction, calibration and enumeration, requested-base evaluation, binding trials and binding gate checks, all ×2, must fit 2,880 core-hours and 15 OC wall days. Workers are fixed at 8, with no reduction. Locked memory fit is 8 × max(locked-size peak RSS of construction, calibration, and trial worker plus helper), using the existing lifetime high-water method, ≤ hw.memsize − 8 GiB (60,129,542,144 bytes on this host). Failed or unmeasured CPU or memory fit means not testable before dev. Locked remeasurement is one create-once run, on the host that will run the binding OC (record hw.model, hw.memsize, logical CPU count and OS build), of the reviewed benchmark and calibration commands with the revision-7 replicate structure (README benchmark invocation `--method studentized --trials 2000 --cores 8` with its cell set and one/two-worker equality; the calibration-overhead command's per-population measurements and worst-case enumeration), changing only the size source to the locked sizes; that size input is the only permitted code change and is reviewed under rule 5. Record load averages and concurrent-process count in provenance. Rerun only after a recorded integrity failure: a crash not caused by resource exhaustion, a closure mismatch, or a host fault evidenced by a contemporaneous OS-recorded malfunction independent of observed timings or partial results; record the reason and preserve that evidence and the interrupted run's available output. A resource-exhaustion crash is a failed fit. Operator termination and host load are not integrity failures; a run terminated without a qualifying integrity failure leaves the fit unmeasured. A failed fit never permits a rerun. Report every completed run; each binding input is the maximum over all completed runs.
safety_scheduling_sentence: The descriptive-safety scheduling policy (start, worker allocation, pauses and termination) is frozen with the reviewed stage-3 OC controller before the first safety output; none of these may depend on partial or completed safety outcomes, and every pause or termination is recorded with its cause.
